raw.assessment: The incumbent already produces the required CSV within 40–75 seconds, and unchanged-assignment centers need a median seven minutes of handling: this limiting observation argues against a universal export-performance problem. Overall, intended-course coverage is 80% versus the 95% target, and median handling is 17 versus 12 minutes. Assignment changes and renames concentrate the observed failures but do not establish causes. Zero sampled cross-center rows is encouraging, with the split-course center explicitly untested. Replacement delay is measured separately from handling time; its contribution to handling remains unknown.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a historical week may exclude courses that belonged in that week’s export; effective-week course membership could prevent these omissions.
openings.delta: Test historical selection semantics before changing job speed or scheduling.
openings.prediction: With identical fabricated attendance, changing only an instructor assignment after attendance entry changes historical export membership under the incumbent; a week-aware selector retains the intended courses.
openings.probe: In staging, reproduce a within-week reassignment against an unchanged control and a predefined intended course set. Compare current selection with a minimal week-aware prototype. Retain the documented CSV, center-scoped authorization, and concurrent attendance entry. Proceed to a bounded change only if required history exists and the six-day and hosting limits hold.
assumptions: Assignment semantics actually affect export membership.
Reliable effective dates or equivalent history are available without a costly migration.

openings.claim: For renamed courses, are records missing, or do coordinators fail to recognize present records against their schedules?
openings.delta: Separate selection failure from name reconciliation using an observable row-presence discriminator.
openings.prediction: A recognition problem leaves every intended fabricated attendance record present while coordinators report an absent course; a selection problem produces objectively absent records.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions with six consenting coordinators to compare unchanged and renamed fabricated courses against supplied timetables. Reconcile expected records inside staging and time checking, correcting, downloading, and importing separately. Keep the CSV schema unchanged and cap this diagnostic within the shared six engineer-days.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate the relevant coordinator reconciliation steps.
The documented schema permits reconciliation against known fabricated attendance records.

raw.assessment: Changes correlate with affected exports; causation and historical data availability remain unproved. These hypotheses convert disruption into control signals without establishing the success thresholds.

openings.claim: Use assignment and rename events to flag the affected center/week for course-set reconciliation. Potentially disruptive mutations become targeted warnings.
openings.delta: Maintain stable course identifiers in a private weekly manifest; request confirmation for changed courses before generating the documented CSV.
openings.prediction: Event-assisted reconciliation catches omitted intended courses in fabricated reassignment and rename cases, while unchanged cases require no added review.
openings.probe: Replay identical fabricated weeks through current selection and event-assisted reconciliation; compare intended identifiers and review time. Include splits, center-isolation checks and attendance entry during preparation.
assumptions: Mutation capture and manifests fit six engineer-days and existing hosting.
Failure boundary: missing past events, ambiguous splits or incorrect confirmation prevent reliable reconstruction.
Data remain private and center-authorized; recording and review do not block attendance entry.

openings.claim: Convert a missing-course report into an explicit center/week selection correction and immediate regeneration request: detected failure supplies the replacement export's selection control.
openings.delta: Replace an unstructured request with an authorized course picker and remembered weekly selection, avoiding unchanged reruns of a possibly defective selector.
openings.prediction: Explicit corrections produce usable replacements sooner; handling time improves only if identifying and confirming corrections is sufficiently cheap.
openings.probe: Have consenting coordinators repair fabricated mismatches using both workflows across their two sessions. Measure checking, correction, download and import separately; verify intended courses, documented CSV, concurrent entry and tenant boundaries.
assumptions: Private authorized regeneration fits six engineer-days and existing hosting.
Failure boundary: stale timetables, absent identities or ambiguous splits undermine corrections; the picker must never widen center access.
The 40–75 second job duration does not establish end-to-end replacement latency.

openings.claim: Historical membership may require effective-week assignments.
openings.discriminator: Reassignment alone changes historical course inclusion.
openings.probe: Compare current and week-aware selection against an unchanged fabricated control.
openings.uncertainty: Causation and affordable reliable history unproved.

openings.claim: Renames may impair recognition or selection.
openings.discriminator: Reported omissions with present records indicate recognition; absent records indicate selection.
openings.probe: Observe six coordinators matching unchanged/renamed fabricated records to timetables; time handling stages.
openings.uncertainty: Task realism and schema reconciliation adequacy unproved.

openings.claim: Mutation events could trigger center/week reconciliation using stable-ID private manifests and pre-export confirmation.
openings.discriminator: Changed cases improve without adding unchanged-case review.
openings.probe: Replay reassignments, renames and splits; compare intended IDs and review time.
openings.uncertainty: Missing events, ambiguous splits or incorrect confirmations defeat reconstruction; cost unproved.

openings.claim: An authorized picker could remember center/week corrections and request immediate regeneration.
openings.discriminator: Usable replacements arrive sooner; handling improves only with cheap correction.
openings.probe: Compare report-repair workflows in coordinator sessions; separately time checking, correction, download and import.
openings.uncertainty: Stale timetables, absent identities and splits undermine corrections; job duration excludes replacement latency.

post_distill.decision: Probe D1/D2 first using staging and six coordinators, two short sessions each. All probes preserve privacy/center authorization, documented CSV and concurrent entry; share six engineer-days and existing hosting. Verify split-center isolation: sampled zero leaks is incomplete. Fast jobs and seven-minute unchanged-case handling weaken universal speed explanations. Synthetic observations prove no mechanism; assess next 40 exports against 12-minute median, 95% intended sets and zero foreign-center records.
